title: Oxidation Number
content: The oxidation number (or oxidation state) of an atom represents the number of electrons lost or gained by an atom and can be zero, positive, or negative.
e: The oxidation number (or oxidation state) of an atom represents the number of electrons lost or gained by an atom and can be zero, positive, or negative. Free elements are assigned oxidation number 0, whether the molecule is monoatomic or diatomic. A positive oxidation number means that atom is assigned fewer electrons than the neutral atom.

title: Oxidation
content: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or electronegative element) to a substance or the removal of hydrogen (or electropositive element) from a substance. It is the loss of electrons by an element, compound or ion, or an increase in oxidation number.
e: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or electronegative element) to a substance or the removal of hydrogen (or electropositive element) from a substance. It is the loss of electrons by an element, compound or ion, or an increase in oxidation number.

title: Reduction
content: Reduction is the removal of oxygen (or electronegative element) from a substance or the addition of hydrogen (or electropositive element) to a substance. It is the gain of electrons by an element, compound or ion, or a decrease in oxidation number.
e: Reduction is the removal of oxygen (or electronegative element) from a substance or the addition of hydrogen (or electropositive element) to a substance. It is the gain of electrons by an element, compound or ion, or a decrease in oxidation number.

title: Redox Reaction
content: Chemical reactions which involve oxidation as well as reduction processes simultaneously are known as redox reactions.
e: Chemical reactions which involve oxidation as well as reduction processes simultaneously are known as redox reactions. Redox is electron transfer: oxidation is loss of electrons and reduction is gain of electrons.

title: Oxidising Agent
content: An oxidising agent or oxidant is an acceptor of electrons and is reduced itself in a chemical reaction.
e: An oxidising agent or oxidant is an acceptor of electrons and is reduced itself in a chemical reaction. An oxidising agent is the species that is reduced. it takes electrons from something else. Oxidising Agent is the word this version is asking about.

title: Reducing Agent
content: A reducing agent or reductant is a donor of electrons and is oxidised in a chemical reaction.
e: A reducing agent or reductant is a donor of electrons and is oxidised in a chemical reaction. A reducing agent is the species that is oxidised. it gives electrons to something else.
